title: Graphs
summary: A graph stores items as nodes and connections as edges.
refresher: A graph is made of nodes and edges. Use a visited set so traversal does not loop forever when edges lead back to a node you already saw.

sections.title: Nodes, edges, and neighbors
sections.summary: A graph can be stored as each node mapped to its neighbors.

blocks.body: A graph does not have one required starting shape like a list. Most coding problems give you edges or a neighbor list. Your first job is to know how to ask: from this node, where can I go next?

blocks.caption: An adjacency list maps each node to the nodes beside it.

blocks.prompt: What does an adjacency list store?
blocks.why: The neighbor list tells traversal where it can move next.

sections.title: Use a visited set
sections.summary: Visited prevents repeated work and infinite loops.

blocks.body: Graphs can have cycles. A cycle means you can follow edges and come back to a node you already visited. Without a visited set, DFS or BFS may repeat forever.

blocks.caption: Mark a node when you decide to visit it.
blocks.right: if neighbor not in visited: visit(neighbor)

blocks.prompt: Why do graph traversals need a visited set?
choices: To avoid visiting the same node again
blocks.why: Visited keeps traversal from repeating nodes, especially in cycles.
